topics.label: Introduction and learning objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This opening frames the lecture on cancer causation and sets out what students should learn.

topics.label: Mutations, clonal evolution and cancer susceptibility
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how mutations can produce cancer through clonal evolution within a susceptible cell and a permissive microenvironment.

topics.label: Environmental contributions to cancer risk
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how environmental exposures contribute to cancer risk rather than attributing cancer solely to chance or inherited susceptibility.

topics.label: Infectious agents in cancer development
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how infections can drive cancer, using Burkitt lymphoma as a detailed example of cooperating infectious causes.

topics.label: Mechanisms of exposure-induced DNA damage
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics trace how environmental carcinogens produce DNA damage that can become mutations.

topics.label: Tumour initiation and promotion
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics distinguish mutation-producing initiation from promotion that enables initiated cells to proliferate and form tumours.

topics.label: Tissue and developmental susceptibility to carcinogens
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how the context of exposure determines carcinogenic effects, ending with a recap that situates this specificity within the mechanisms already discussed.

topics.label: Investigating carcinogen exposure and carcinogenicity
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how evidence of carcinogenic exposure and activity can be obtained and what limits its interpretation.

topics.label: Closing summary and risk–benefit decisions
topics.groupedBecause: This closing draws together the lecture's conclusions about environmental cancer risks and the difficulty of assessing them for everyday risk–benefit decisions.
